detail.runner_up_case: NO_ADVERSE is defensible on this file as it stands, though not comfortably. The ADVERSE case rests entirely on the 2017 EDNY securities-fraud/conspiracy conviction, but the only direct evidence in the file is secondary: a third-party Bureau-of-Prisons roster aggregator (federalcriminaldefenseattorney.com) and a user-edited Wikidata description ('convicted felon'), while the court_records hit is a 2017 severance-motion opinion, not a judgment of conviction or an appellate mandate confirming the conviction remains final and unvacated as of 2026-10-01. Q4 is genuinely open, and not hypothetically so: Shkreli publicly and repeatedly sought a presidential pardon (reported through 2025), and Q3's own framing treats a pardoned or vacated conviction as no longer on record. His punishment is complete (released September 14, 2022) with no post-release criminal charge documented in the file. If a pardon or vacatur were found AND the December 2021 FTC v. Vyera judgment (~$64.6M plus a lifetime pharmaceutical-industry ban) were reversed on appeal, the remaining record — a completed sentence, business disputes, and the Wu-Tang album litigation — would fall below the materiality bar, and with identity firmly established (Wikidata Q6776585, b. 1983-03-17, ex-CEO Turing, founder Retrophin), the verdict would be NO_ADVERSE. The honest caveat: this is one of the most publicized white-collar convictions of the decade, and the FTC judgment alone would independently sustain ADVERSE even if the conviction were pardoned, so NO_ADVERSE requires neutralizing both prongs with primary, dated evidence — a high bar the current file does not meet, which is why ADVERSE remains the leading verdict.
